name: Allan Alcorn
milestone_by_age_26: Designed and engineered Atari's arcade game Pong, released November 29, 1972, at age 24—one of the first commercially successful video games and a foundational product of the industry.
early_history_summary: Born January 1, 1948, in San Francisco. Earned a B.S. in EECS from UC Berkeley in 1971, worked at Ampex where he met Ted Dabney and others in the nascent video engineering community, then joined Atari as an early engineer under Nolan Bushnell. Assigned Pong as a training exercise, he built a polished arcade design that became Atari's breakout hit.
family_context_summary: Born in San Francisco; second child in family; limited public detail beyond local upbringing and Berkeley path.
primary_early_advantage_tags: UC Berkeley EECS, Ampex, Silicon Valley video, Atari, Nolan Bushnell, arcade hardware
evidence_summary: Allan Alcorn (b. 1948) designed Pong at Atari in 1972 at age 24 after Berkeley EECS and Ampex experience. Pong's arcade release made him a defining early video-game engineer; he later worked on Atari platforms, hired Steve Jobs, and consulted across Silicon Valley. Advantages were primarily Bay Area technical ecosystem proximity, Ampex/Atari peer networks, and scarce digital video/game hardware skill for the era rather than family capital or inherited audience.
starting_point: Born January 1, 1948, in San Francisco; raised locally and trained in electrical engineering at UC Berkeley.
current_position: Living pioneering video-game engineer known as Pong's designer; longtime Silicon Valley consultant, former Apple Fellow, and public historian of Atari-era computing.

trajectory.event: Earned B.S. in EECS from UC Berkeley and entered industry engineering roles.
Designed Atari's Pong, released as a commercial arcade hit on November 29, 1972.
Hired Steve Jobs at Atari and continued as a core engineer on early Atari products.
Helped advance home Pong and broader Atari consumer video-game hardware.
Left Atari after internal product conflicts and began Silicon Valley consulting and startup advising.
Co-founded Silicon Gaming, applying computer graphics technology to wagering machines.
Co-founded Zowie Intertainment; the company was later acquired by Lego.

name: Matt Corallo
milestone_by_age_26: Began contributing to Bitcoin Core in early 2011 while still in high school (~age 18), becoming one of the earliest active post-Satoshi Core developers; implemented wallet private-key encryption merged mid-2011 (PRs #232/#352).
early_history_summary: As a high-school student (in Germany near Frankfurt per interviews), Corallo discovered Bitcoin via technical podcasts around late 2010–early 2011, then rapidly became an active open-source contributor under TheBlueMatt. He later studied computer science at UNC Chapel Hill (2011–2014), co-founded Blockstream (2014), and built major Bitcoin infrastructure including relay networks, FIBRE, and the Lightning Development Kit.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bitcoin Core, open source, high school contributor, Blockstream, Lightning, Spiral
evidence_summary: Matt Corallo entered Bitcoin Core development in early 2011 as a high-schooler (~age 18 per interviews) and landed material early contributions such as wallet encryption. He co-founded Blockstream in 2014, created FIBRE and later LDK/rust-lightning, and has worked full-time on Bitcoin/Lightning at Chaincode and Spiral. Early advantage is primarily platform-native open-source immersion and scarce protocol skill during Bitcoin's formative wave; family background is undocumented. Birth year estimated ~1992 from age-18 statements around 2010–2011 (CSV listed 1988, which conflicts with high-school timing).
starting_point: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond high-school student in Germany near Frankfurt when entering Bitcoin development.
current_position: Open-source engineer at Spiral (Block) focused on Bitcoin Core and Lightning (LDK); long-time Bitcoin protocol contributor and former Blockstream co-founder.

trajectory.event: Started contributing to Bitcoin Core in high school; wallet private-key encryption work merged mid-2011.
Co-implemented micro-payment channels in bitcoinj, an early practical Lightning precursor.
Co-founded Blockstream and co-authored the pegged sidechains white paper after UNC CS studies.
Released FIBRE, a near-speed-of-light Bitcoin block relay protocol used by miners.
Began rust-lightning / Lightning Development Kit as a modular Lightning SDK.
Joined Square Crypto (later Spiral) as a full-time open-source Bitcoin engineer after Chaincode Labs.

name: Jeremy Stoppelman
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Yelp in summer 2004 (commonly dated July 2004) with Russel Simmons after a doctor-search problem during flu, with $1M seed from Max Levchin—while still age 26 (born November 10, 1977).
early_history_summary: Born in Arlington, Virginia, to an English-teacher mother and securities-lawyer father. Programmed as a teen, invested in stocks at 14, studied computer engineering at UIUC (B.S. 1999), joined X.com/PayPal and rose to VP of Engineering, then left after eBay's acquisition for Harvard Business School. During a 2004 summer internship at MRL Ventures he co-founded Yelp.
family_context_summary: Born in Arlington, Virginia; mother Lynn was an English teacher and father John a securities lawyer; Jewish family background; brother Michael later worked at Yelp.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a securities lawyer (professional/legal domain, not local reviews tech); mother taught English. No direct product-domain apprenticeship documented.

evidence_summary: Jeremy Stoppelman (b. 1977) co-founded Yelp at age 26 after PayPal VP Engineering experience and a Harvard Business School year. Seed came from PayPal peer Max Levchin; co-founder Russel Simmons was a former PayPal colleague. Advantages include elite institutional pipeline (UIUC, HBS), Silicon Valley/PayPal network capital, and a complementary technical cofounder more than family domain inheritance. He remains Yelp CEO after taking the company public in 2012.
starting_point: Born November 10, 1977, in Arlington, Virginia, to an English-teacher mother and securities-lawyer father; middle-class professional household with early computer and investing interest.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Yelp; public company leader and housing/antitrust advocate based in the Bay Area.

trajectory.event: Graduated UIUC in computer engineering and entered industry, soon joining X.com/PayPal.
